title: The Spark Is Burning Metal: Lanthanoids in Everyday Technology
subject: Chemistry
objective: A lighter "flint" is not stone but mischmetall, about 95% lanthanoid metals (mostly cerium) and 5% iron; scraped shavings catch fire in air, so the spark is burning metal. Lanthanoids are silvery-white, soft metals that tarnish rapidly in air; hardness increases with atomic number (samarium is steel-hard); they conduct heat and electricity. They are very reactive (early members like calcium, later ones like aluminium; E° about −2.2 to −2.4 V): they burn in O₂ (Ln₂O₃; Ce gives CeO₂) and halogens (LnX₃), react with water (Ln(OH)₃ + H₂) and dilute acids (H₂), and on heating form LnN, Ln₂S₃, LnC₂ (2773 K) and hydrides. Their oxides and hydroxides are basic. Most Ln³⁺ ions are coloured because of f electrons; La³⁺ (4f⁰) and Lu³⁺ (4f¹⁴) are colourless. Uses: alloy steels (best single use), mischmetall in Mg alloys for bullets, shells and lighter flint, mixed oxides as petroleum-cracking catalysts, oxides as TV phosphors, and Nd₂Fe₁₄B magnets in phones. Rare earths are not rare: cerium is as common as copper.

tf.q: Lanthanoid metals are hard and do not tarnish in air.
tf.explain: They are soft and tarnish rapidly.

tf.q: Hardness of the lanthanoids increases with atomic number.

tf.explain: They are basic, like alkaline-earth hydroxides.

tf.q: Lanthanoids liberate hydrogen from dilute acids.
Rare earths are rarer in the crust than silver.
tf.explain: Even thulium (~0.5 ppm) beats silver (~0.075 ppm).

ar.a: Assertion: La³⁺ and Lu³⁺ are colourless. Reason: they have 4f⁰ and 4f¹⁴ configurations.
ar.r: Both true; the reason explains the assertion: no f–f excitation is possible.

ar.a: Assertion: The sparks of a lighter are burning metal. Reason: shavings of cerium alloy ignite in air at only about 150–180 °C.
ar.r: Both true; the reason explains the assertion.

short.q: Write balanced equations for a lanthanoid (Ln) reacting with (a) oxygen, (b) chlorine.
Write the products of a lanthanoid heated with N₂, S, C (2773 K) and H₂.
short.solution: LnN; Ln₂S₃; LnC₂ (also Ln₃C, Ln₂C₃); a hydride such as LnH₂.

short.q: Give four uses of the lanthanoids.
short.solution: Alloy steels for plates and pipes; mischmetall in Mg alloys for bullets, shells and lighter flint; mixed oxides as petroleum-cracking catalysts; oxides as phosphors in TV screens.

right: ≈ 95 % Ln + ≈ 5 % Fe (+ S, C, Ca, Al)
